patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Brevo and Kit share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Brevo only if your buying job matches “Multi-channel email marketing with send-based pricing, a generous free plan, and CRM-lite ” rather than Kit's shape. Choose Kit only if your buying job matches “Creator and newsletter ESP (formerly ConvertKit) with landing pages, automations, and digi” rather than Brevo's shape. Workflow advantage: Brevo leans ecommerce-email; Kit leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Brevo and Kit share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Brevo is Multi-channel email marketing with send-based pricing, a generous free plan, and CRM-lite tools — formerly Sendinblue.; Kit is Creator and newsletter ESP (formerly ConvertKit) with landing pages, automations, and digital product selling..
- Company-size focus: Brevo (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Kit (micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Brevo-leaning ecommerce-email vs Kit-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Brevo — Free plan daily send cap (300/day) constrains frequent campaigners; Kit — Free Newsletter plan limits automations vs Creator/Pro.

Limitations — Brevo: Free plan daily send cap (300/day) constrains frequent campaigners; Advanced automation and A/B depth concentrate on Standard+; Kit: Free Newsletter plan limits automations vs Creator/Pro; Paid pricing scales with subscribers.

Poor-fit cases: Brevo is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free plan daily send cap (300/day) constrains frequent campaigners · Kit is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free Newsletter plan limits automations vs Creator/Pro · Avoid Brevo if you actually need Kit's motion (Creator and newsletter ESP (formerly ConvertKit) with landing pages, automations)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
